1.why: MFA endpoints use authenticated() and accountFor(session.userId) only; body userId/accountId fields are rejected by forbiddenIdentity/csrfValid.

2.why: Identity OTPs are bound to the session’s identityHash, TOTP/recovery material to the account map—codes do not validate for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets account.mfaEnabled and issues recovery codes; no other sessions are destroyed or forced to re-authenticate.

4.why: totpSecret is stored via AES-GCM encryptValue; recovery codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes in recoveryCodes.

5.why: Secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, OTPs, and recovery codes all come from crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie writes for secrets/OTPs/tokens.

7.why: Server validates login (normalizedLogin), OTP (safeOtp), recovery (safeRecovery), CSRF shape, body size/keys, and rejects unexpected identity fields.

8.why: UI uses textContent/createElement; API returns JSON; HTML is server-built with CSP nonces—no unencoded reflection of user input.

9.why: validRedirect allow-lists only #/signin, #/identity, #/setup, #/confirmed, #/recovery and sign-in enforces it.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none'.

11.why: sessionCookie sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Generic client errors, no stack traces; secrets not written to server logs or URLs (demo testCode only in JSON body to the owner).

13.why: Identity codes are single-use with identityExpires (5 minutes); TOTP steps recorded in totpUsedSteps; recovery codes marked used.

14.why: sign-in, identity, TOTP, and recovery each use AttemptState with MAX_FAILURES=5 and LOCK_MS lockout.

15.why: Sign-in destroys the old session and creates a new id; idle/absolute timeouts in readSession; logout calls destroySession and expires the cookie.
